their_exact_setting: arXiv:2403.06357 (v2, Jul 2026) Remark 1 restates Lanke 1974 Thm 2: no real-valued locally bounded g_L,g_R on R^n with P(g_L(X)<theta<g_R(X))>1-alpha (open interval, strict coverage) for iid continuous X symmetric about theta, when n<log2(2/alpha). They call Lanke's claim false (eq.(5) a-anchored interval works for n>=log2(1/alpha), not shift-invariant). Conjecture: no shift-invariant, locally bounded CI exists for n<log2(2/alpha). 'Shift-invariant' and 'locally bounded' are not formally defined (natural reading g(x+c1)=g(x)+c; bounded on bounded sets); the class is not restated in the conjecture. Their Thm 1 class: independent X_i with common median (P(X<=t)>=1/2,P(X>=t)>=1/2), closed intervals, coverage>=1-alpha; their shift-invariant order-statistic interval is finite iff n>=log2(2/alpha).
proof_or_gap: The sketch as written is flawed: with a unique median in the near cluster (eps>0) only the far-cluster event forces a miss (g_L>=2theta-M>median); the near-cluster event does not (M=sup_K|g| may exceed 1 so the median can lie inside [-M,M]). That gives only (1/2-eps)^n -> 2^-n, i.e. Lanke's bound. eps<0 just swaps roles. With eps=0 (centre of symmetry, Lanke's class, non-unique median) both events force a miss and the 2^(1-n) argument works. REPAIR that also keeps the median unique: three clusters P_{eta,D}: mass (1-eta)/2 uniform on A=[-1,1], (1-eta)/2 on B=[2D-1,2D+1], eta on C=[D-w,D+w]; continuous, symmetric about D, unique median D for eta>0. With M=max(sup_K|g_L|,sup_K|g_R|), K=[-1,1]^n, D>M: all-in-A => g_R<=M<D miss; all-in-B => X=Y+2D1, g_L(X)=g_L(Y)+2D>=2D-M>D miss. Disjoint, so P(miss)>=2((1-eta)/2)^n -> 2^(1-n) as eta->0. Hence validity (coverage>=1-alpha) forces alpha>=2^(1-n), i.e. n>=log2(2/alpha); the conjecture is true in this formalisation (open or closed intervals; symmetric or unique-median class; in Lanke's strict >1-alpha symmetric class eta=0 is attained so n=log2(2/alpha) is excluded too). Sharp: their Thm-1 interval is shift-invariant and valid for n>=log2(2/alpha). Only g_L bounded below and g_R bounded above on K plus shift equivariance for one shift c=2D are used. Caveats: measurability (bound is on outer probability), randomized intervals not checked, and the result is for my formalisation of 'shift-invariant' since the paper does not define it.
numerical_check: Monte Carlo (4e5 reps, D=1e4, eta=1e-3; provisional, +-~0.001). n=3,4,5: min miss over all order-statistic intervals [X_(i),X_(j)] and mean+-c*range (c=0.5,1,2,5) at theta=D = 0.2488, 0.1245, 0.0622 vs forced bound 2((1-eta)/2)^n = 0.2493, 0.1245, 0.0622; no candidate below the bound. Two-cluster variant confirmed to force only (1/2-eps)^n. Paper's eq.(5) a=0 interval (not shift-invariant), n=3, alpha=0.2 (log2(1/alpha)=2.32<3<3.32): miss 0.1244/0.1258 under three-cluster eta=1e-3/0.2 (<=0.2) while shift-invariant intervals have miss>=0.249>0.2.
novelty: Provisional, screening incomplete. Semantic Scholar citations of 2403.06357 returned only 2 items (a cloud-segmentation paper and arXiv:2401.09379 'Merging uncertainty sets via majority vote'), neither addresses the conjecture; index clearly incomplete, several 429s. Crossref has no record for the preprint. arXiv API boolean queries returned only the paper itself. Several web searches (conjecture wording, Lanke impossibility, finite-population/equivariant median CI) found no paper proving or refuting the conjecture; arXiv v2 (Jul 2026) still states it as conjecture. No finite-population or equivariant version found (finite-population median CIs under SRS exist but are different). Related: Lanke 1974; Kuchibhotla-Balakrishnan-Wasserman arXiv:2206.02954; Paul-Kuchibhotla mode paper arXiv:2503.23711. Conclusion: 'not found taken', not 'verified novel'; the argument is a short cluster/scale device of the same kind as Lanke's, so a later version or an unindexed source may contain it.
